events.title: Portuguese trading fort on Arguin
hints: A reef-ringed island off a desert coast hosted one of Europe's earliest trading posts in tropical Africa.
It bought gum and captives from the desert coast and shipped them to Portugal.
events.summary: Prince Henry the Navigator set up a trading post on Arguin in 1445, buying gum arabic and enslaved people for Portugal. The Dutch captured the island in 1633.

events.title: Brandenburg-Prussian fort on Arguin
hints: A German state tried its hand at colonial trade from a desert island.
It sold enslaved people and traded gum from a small fort.
The post was abandoned in the early 18th century.
events.summary: Brandenburg-Prussia took over a fort on Arguin in the 1680s and used it for trade, including trade in enslaved people, until the post was abandoned in 1721.

events.title: French conquest of the Moorish lands
hints: A French official called Coppolani led a so-called peaceful penetration of a desert emirate region from 1902.
He was killed in 1905, and military conquest followed.
Resistance in the Adrar region ended only in the 1930s.
events.summary: From 1902 Xavier Coppolani led a French drive to take control of the Moorish emirates south of Morocco. After his assassination in 1905 France used armed force, completing the conquest in the 1930s.

events.title: MIFERMA iron ore mines
hints: A consortium led by a European state's companies dug a huge desert iron mine near Zouérat.
A railway across the desert carried ore to the Atlantic coast.
events.summary: The French-led company MIFERMA, founded in 1952, mined iron ore near Zouérat and exported it by a purpose-built railway to the coast. The Mauritanian government nationalised it in 1974.
